To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the rate of ultrashort-pulsed laser mode-locking can be controlled by adjusting the nonlinear absorption properties of the saturable absorber dye.
The best nonlinear absorbers are those having a pure electronic transition near the laser frequency.

the optimal operating regime of a mode-locked laser with a saturable absorber is characterized by the fact that the relaxation times for the bleaching of the absorber and the buildup of the laser pulse in the resonator are comparable.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new type of laser system which is capable of producing ultrashort pulses with a duration of several tens of picoseconds and a peak power of up to 1 GW.
the development of a new generation of tunable lasers for generating ultrashort pulses with durations in the subnanosecond range.
a study of the dynamics of mode-locked lasers with a saturable absorber.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nonlinear optical properties of the dye are the key factor in determining the optimal regime of operation of saturable absorber in mode-locked solid state lasers.
the use of a saturable absorber with the appropriate characteristics can provide a significant improvement in laser mode-locking performance.

the use of a saturable absorber in the form of a jet of dye solution in a mode-locked laser has the following advantages: (1) The saturable absorber can be tuned over a wide range of the laser spectrum, and (2) the absorber is easily pumped by a separate laser.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the best dye is the dye which is closest to the lasing frequency.
we are able to generate 1-10 ps pulses in rhodamine 5G lasers with a 300 nsec pump pulses.

, in the case of a pulsed laser pumping, the best dopes of nonlinear absorber are the ones with purely electronic transition, and in the case of continuous wave (CW) laser pumping, it is the dyes with a mixed electronic and vibrational transitions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nonlinear absorber is a key element for the generation of ultrashort optical pulses in a mode-locked laser.

the optimal regime of operation for the nonlinear absorber in mode-locked laser systems is determined by the ratio of the time of formation of ultrahigh-power pulses to the time of their relaxation in the saturable absorber.
